# Formula functions and types

<!-- Generated by npm run docs:generate. Edit the owning runtime definitions, not this file. -->

This reference is generated from the same definitions that execute formulas and supply editor help. It covers **22 spreadsheet/builder functions**, **43 methods**, and **311 exposed mathjs callables**.

## Conventions and compatibility

- Formula types are structured runtime descriptors, not strings or JavaScript classes available to formulas. Generic variables T, U and A describe relationships; users do not declare types. Known receiver/argument types bind those variables without reading a stream or executing callbacks. Unknown types remain Any.
- Rows and column indexes are zero-based. Ranges, relative/calculated references and named/dataset references resolve against the current workbook. A direct reference to a spill source reads its entire result; a range reads each cell element.
- Number uses 64-significant-digit decimal arithmetic. Display, charts, clipboard and native-number-only mathjs functions retain their existing native-number precision. Blank is empty text, not null and not an empty Optional.
- Arithmetic/comparison broadcasts scalars over arrays; two arrays require matching dimensions. Array-producing formulas spill without overwriting occupied cells. Records and positional stream rows convert to headed tables only at the final cell boundary, not midway through method chains.
- Conditions and numeric conversion are operation-specific; exact lookup-key matching does not use arithmetic coercion. COUNT counts every cell, and AVG/MEAN divide the numeric sum by every cell, including text/blanks. These compatibility rules intentionally differ from Excel and Java.
- Stream.findFirst/min/max/average now return Optional. Migrate a previous numeric result with .orElse(0), or .orElseThrow() to explicitly require a value. Seeded reduce, sum, count, match tests and toTable are not made optional. Existing FILTER/LOOKUP/AVGIF error contracts are unchanged.
- Empty Optionals represent absence only. Invalid data, source errors, division by zero and cycles still propagate. Optional.orElse is lazy like IF, unlike Java's eager orElse. A present blank/zero/FALSE stays present. Unresolved Stream/Optional/Lambda values cannot display, enter scalar arithmetic, become spill fields or pass to ordinary functions. Unwrap an Optional explicitly; IFERROR is not an absence test.
- Lambdas are safe interpreted expressions. Records have read-only literal fields; JavaScript statements, assignments, prototypes and arbitrary methods are unavailable. Inside stream/Optional callbacks and method arguments, + concatenates when either operand is text; ordinary arithmetic outside those expressions is unchanged.
- A function can fail in addition to returning its documented type. Wrong arity/type, reference/domain errors and source errors propagate. #SPILL! means occupied/overlapping/out-of-sheet output; #VALUE! means invalid values/shapes; #REF! means invalid reference; #N/A means a required value is missing; #CALC! means an invalid/oversized array result. Circular references cannot be hidden by IFERROR or fallbacks.

## Formula types

<a id="type-Any"></a>
### Any

An unconstrained formula value. A concrete runtime value still has a type; this is not permission to access JavaScript properties.

<a id="type-Number"></a>
### Number

A real number. Decimal arithmetic retains 64 significant digits internally. Display, charts and native-number-only library functions use native-number precision. Infinity and NaN are numeric values where the operation permits them.

<a id="type-Text"></a>
### Text

Case-sensitive text. Blank cells and empty text both evaluate to ""; neither is Optional.empty.

<a id="type-Boolean"></a>
### Boolean

TRUE or FALSE. Spreadsheet conditions additionally accept numeric and boolean-like text through explicit condition conversion.

<a id="type-Complex"></a>
### Complex

A mathjs complex number. Supported by compatible mathematical functions, not by exact lookup keys or chart series.

<a id="type-Unit"></a>
### Unit

A mathjs quantity with units. Use compatible math functions and unit conversion; not an exact lookup key or chart value.

<a id="type-Fraction"></a>
### Fraction

A mathjs exact fraction. Available to compatible mathematical functions; spreadsheet numeric conversion and key rules are documented per function.

<a id="type-BigInt"></a>
### BigInt

A mathjs/native arbitrary-precision integer, distinct from the default decimal Number. Only compatible mathematical functions accept it.

<a id="type-Scalar"></a>
### Scalar

A single Number, Text, Boolean, Complex, Unit, Fraction or BigInt value. Arrays and expression-only values are not scalars.

<a id="type-NumericInput"></a>
### NumericInput

A Number, Boolean, or numeric/blank Text accepted by spreadsheet numeric conversion. TRUE/FALSE become 1/0; blank becomes 0. Other text errors. Conversion is explicit in the operation, not implicit Optional unwrapping.

<a id="type-Condition"></a>
### Condition

A scalar condition: Boolean, Number, blank, TRUE/FALSE text or numeric text. Blank/zero/FALSE are false; other nonnumeric text errors.

<a id="type-Array"></a>
### Array

A rectangular two-dimensional array. Scalars can be promoted to 1×1 arrays by array functions. Array results spill; 1×1 results display as a scalar. Shapes must match unless scalar broadcasting is documented.

<a id="type-Row"></a>
### Row

A positional single-row array, used as one stream item. A row projection receives column1, column2, … headings unless overridden.

<a id="type-Table"></a>
### Table

A headed rectangular array. The first row contains headings, including when there are no data rows. Object keys supply headings; table fields must be scalar. Normal spill collision and boundary checks apply.

<a id="type-Record"></a>
### Record

An immutable record with named fields. Stream headings and object projections define its schema. Field names are case-sensitive; access uses a.name or a["Last Name"]. At the cell boundary a record becomes a headed one-row table.

<a id="type-Stream"></a>
### Stream

A lazy sequence of items, created from headed ranges. A terminal operation is mandatory. Filter/map/limit/skip use generators; sorting buffers; distinct stores seen keys. Source errors propagate when read.

<a id="type-Optional"></a>
### Optional

Either one present value or empty. Zero, FALSE and empty text are present. Missing stream results are empty; invalid input and calculation errors still propagate. Explicitly unwrap before display, arithmetic, table fields or ordinary function arguments. map/filter do not invoke callbacks when empty. Unlike Java, orElse evaluates its fallback only when empty, like spreadsheet IF.

<a id="type-Lambda"></a>
### Lambda

An interpreted expression callback, written a->expression or (a,b)->expression. Parameters are lexically scoped. No statements, mutation, JavaScript execution, arbitrary methods or prototype access. Callback arity is validated by its consumer.

<a id="type-Chart"></a>
### Chart

A declarative CHART() builder rendered over the grid. It occupies one formula cell, not spill cells. A builder without a chart type displays blank; a typed builder needs a series. Chart arguments are restricted literals/references, not general expressions. Charts cannot be numeric formula inputs.

<a id="type-ConditionalRule"></a>
### ConditionalRule

A declarative CF() builder applied through the conditional-format pane. It requires a local absolute range and foreground/background/alignment. A predicate is evaluated per target cell; rules are not scalar cell data.

<a id="type-Reference"></a>
### Reference

A cell, range or named/dataset reference. This describes argument syntax, not a separately stored cell value. Resolution reads values in the current workbook context. Builder methods document which reference forms they accept.

<a id="type-MathValue"></a>
### MathValue

An additional mathjs value (for example ResultSet). Only compatible library overloads accept it. No arbitrary property/method access is permitted. Library-specific values display using their existing string representation.

<a id="type-Math.LibraryCallback"></a>
### Math.LibraryCallback

A JavaScript callback required by a mathjs overload. Not available in formulas: formula lambdas are safe interpreted objects, not JavaScript functions. Use Stream/Optional callback methods instead.

<a id="type-Math.ConfigOptions"></a>
### Math.ConfigOptions

An upstream mathjs type. Produced and consumed by compatible library functions; general JavaScript object construction and property access are unavailable.

<a id="type-Math.Record"></a>

## Spreadsheet and builder functions

<a id="function-rowstream"></a>
### rowstream

Read a range or array as headed records. The first row supplies unique nonblank text field names; remaining rows are read lazily. No terminal operation is implied.

**rowstream**(rangeIncludingHeadings: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Stream](#type-Stream)&lt;[Record](#type-Record)&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rangeIncludingHeadings | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid headings or source shape; source/reference errors propagate when read.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("age",23,19)).toTable()
```

<a id="function-SUM"></a>
### SUM

Sum numeric values across all cells in all arguments. Text and blanks are ignored; booleans count as 1/0. Ordinary real inputs return Number; compatible mathjs numeric values retain their numeric type. Unlike Stream.sum, numeric text literals are not converted.

**SUM**(…values: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Scalar](#type-Scalar)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| values (variadic) | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Source errors propagate; charts and unresolved expression values are not numeric inputs.

**Examples:**

```text
=SUM(0.1,0.2)
=SUM(VSTACK(2,"ignored",3))
```

<a id="function-COUNT"></a>
### COUNT

Count all cells, including text and blanks. This preserves DataFlow compatibility, not Excel numeric-only COUNT.

**COUNT**(…values: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Number](#type-Number)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| values (variadic) | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=COUNT(VSTACK(2,"", "text"))
```

<a id="function-AVG"></a>
### AVG

Divide SUM by COUNT of all supplied cells, including text/blanks in the divisor. Ordinary real inputs return Number; compatible mathjs numeric inputs retain their numeric type. This is not Stream.average and does not return Optional.

**AVG**(…values: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Scalar](#type-Scalar)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| values (variadic) | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=AVG(VSTACK(2,"",4))
```

<a id="function-MEAN"></a>
### MEAN

Alias of AVG: numeric sum divided by every supplied cell, including text/blanks. Returns Number for ordinary real inputs.

**MEAN**(…values: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Scalar](#type-Scalar)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| values (variadic) | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=MEAN(2,4)
```

<a id="function-SUMIF"></a>
### SUMIF

Sum numeric values whose corresponding condition matches criteria. Omitted valueRange uses conditionRange. Flattened input cell counts must match. Criteria accept =, <>, !=, !, <, >, <=, >= and legacy unquoted syntax; no range-valued criteria. Text values are ignored, booleans count as 1/0.

**SUMIF**(conditionRange: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, criteria: [Scalar](#type-Scalar), valueRange?: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Scalar](#type-Scalar)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| conditionRange | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| criteria | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) | Required | See behavior above. |
| valueRange | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Optional; see behavior | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: mismatched cell counts; source errors propagate.

**Examples:**

```text
=SUMIF(VSTACK(1,3),">1",VSTACK(10,20))
```

<a id="function-COUNTIF"></a>
### COUNTIF

Count cells matching the same comparison criteria as SUMIF. The optional legacy third argument is accepted but not evaluated or used.

**COUNTIF**(conditionRange: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, criteria: [Scalar](#type-Scalar), legacyIgnoredRange?: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Number](#type-Number)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| conditionRange | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| criteria | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) | Required | See behavior above. |
| legacyIgnoredRange | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Optional; see behavior | See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=COUNTIF(VSTACK(1,3),">1")
```

<a id="function-AVGIF"></a>
### AVGIF

Divide the matching numeric sum by the number of matching conditions, including matches with nonnumeric values. Omitted valueRange uses conditionRange. Criteria and flattened dimensions follow SUMIF. Does not return Optional.

**AVGIF**(conditionRange: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, criteria: [Scalar](#type-Scalar), valueRange?: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Scalar](#type-Scalar)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| conditionRange | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| criteria | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) | Required | See behavior above. |
| valueRange | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Optional; see behavior | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #DIV/0!: no matches; #VALUE!: mismatched cell counts.

**Examples:**

```text
=AVGIF(VSTACK(1,3),">1",VSTACK(10,20))
```

<a id="function-IF"></a>
### IF

Evaluate only the branch selected by one scalar condition. Omitted whenFalse returns FALSE. Branches may return different types or arrays; the return type is their union. Errors in unused branches are not evaluated.

**IF**(condition: [Condition](#type-Condition), whenTrue: `T`, whenFalse?: `U`) → `T` ∣ `U` ∣ [Boolean](#type-Boolean)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| condition | [Condition](#type-Condition) | Required | See behavior above. |
| whenTrue | `T` | Required | Lazy; only evaluated if needed. See behavior above. |
| whenFalse | `U` | Optional; see behavior | Lazy; only evaluated if needed. See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: array condition or invalid condition conversion.

**Examples:**

```text
=IF(TRUE,7,1/0)
```

<a id="function-IFERROR"></a>
### IFERROR

Evaluate value, using fallback only if evaluation fails. Error-looking text is not an error. Cycles and aborted evaluations cannot be hidden. This handles errors, not empty Optionals.

**IFERROR**(value: `T`, fallback: `U`) → `T` ∣ `U`

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `T` | Required | Lazy; only evaluated if needed. See behavior above. |
| fallback | `U` | Required | Lazy; only evaluated if needed. See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=IFERROR(1/0,"Unavailable")
```

<a id="function-FILTER"></a>
### FILTER

Keep rows with a true mask value, in source order. Include must be one column or one row with exactly one condition per input row. Scalars promote to 1×1 arrays. Headers are ordinary rows. Fallback evaluates only if no rows match; without it no matches is an error, not Optional.empty.

**FILTER**(array: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, include: [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt;, ifEmpty?: `U`) → [Array](#type-Array)&lt;`T`&gt; ∣ `U`

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| array | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| include | [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| ifEmpty | `U` | Optional; see behavior | Lazy; only evaluated if needed. See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid mask dimensions; #CALC!: no matches without ifEmpty; #SPILL!: occupied or out-of-sheet output.

**Examples:**

```text
=FILTER(VSTACK(2,5),VSTACK(FALSE,TRUE))
```

<a id="function-LOOKUP"></a>
### LOOKUP

Return one values row per query key row, preserving query order. Key widths must match; sourceKeys and values need the same height. Multiple key columns form exact composite keys. Text is case/whitespace sensitive; numeric decimals match exactly; blank components never match. A missing-key fallback is a scalar filling the row, or a 1×output-width row, evaluated only if needed. Duplicate matches are errors even with a fallback. A 1×1 result displays as a scalar. Maximum output: 1,000,000 cells.

**LOOKUP**(queryKeys: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, sourceKeys: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, values: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, ifMissing?: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Array](#type-Array)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| queryKeys | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| sourceKeys | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| values | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| ifMissing | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Optional; see behavior | Lazy; only evaluated if needed. See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #N/A: missing key without fallback; #VALUE!: duplicate matches, invalid keys/shapes/fallback; #CALC!: result too large; source and spill errors propagate.

**Examples:**

```text
=LOOKUP("P2",VSTACK("P1","P2"),VSTACK(10,20))
```

<a id="function-JOIN"></a>
### JOIN

Return all matching pairs: left columns followed by right columns, in left then right source order. Data/key heights and key widths must match. Exact composite-key semantics follow LOOKUP. Duplicate keys produce every pair. Kind "left" keeps unmatched left rows padded with blanks; "inner" omits them. No sorting or deduplication. Headers are ordinary rows. Maximum output: 1,000,000 cells.

**JOIN**(left: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, leftKeys: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, right: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, rightKeys: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, kind?: [Text](#type-Text)) → [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| left | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| leftKeys | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| right | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| rightKeys | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| kind | [Text](#type-Text) | Default: `"left"` | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid kind, keys or shapes; #CALC!: no inner matches or output too large; source and spill errors propagate.

**Examples:**

```text
=JOIN(VSTACK("a","b"),VSTACK(1,2),"x",2)
```

<a id="function-VSTACK"></a>
### VSTACK

Stack arrays vertically in argument order. Scalars promote to 1×1. Every input must have the same width; no padding or implicit headers.

**VSTACK**(…array: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| array (variadic) | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: incompatible widths; normal spill protection applies.

**Examples:**

```text
=VSTACK(2,5)
```

<a id="function-HSTACK"></a>
### HSTACK

Stack arrays horizontally in argument order. Scalars promote to 1×1. Every input must have the same height; no padding or implicit headers.

**HSTACK**(…array: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| array (variadic) | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: incompatible heights; normal spill protection applies.

**Examples:**

```text
=HSTACK(2,5)
```

<a id="function-AND"></a>
### AND

Combine conditions elementwise with AND. All arguments evaluate; scalars broadcast, while arrays must have the same shape. Uses spreadsheet condition conversion, not JavaScript truthiness.

**AND**(…condition: [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt;) → [Boolean](#type-Boolean) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Boolean](#type-Boolean)&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| condition (variadic) | [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid condition or shape mismatch.

**Examples:**

```text
=AND(VSTACK(TRUE,FALSE),TRUE)
```

<a id="function-OR"></a>
### OR

Combine conditions elementwise with OR. All arguments evaluate; scalars broadcast and arrays require the same shape.

**OR**(…condition: [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt;) → [Boolean](#type-Boolean) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Boolean](#type-Boolean)&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| condition (variadic) | [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid condition or shape mismatch.

**Examples:**

```text
=OR(FALSE,TRUE)
```

<a id="function-NOT"></a>
### NOT

Invert a scalar condition or every element of a condition array, preserving shape.

**NOT**(condition: [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt;) → [Boolean](#type-Boolean) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Boolean](#type-Boolean)&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| condition | [Condition](#type-Condition) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Condition](#type-Condition)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid condition conversion.

**Examples:**

```text
=NOT(FALSE)
```

<a id="function-SORT"></a>
### SORT

Stable row sort by a zero-based column index within the array. Order is 1 ascending or -1 descending; blanks are always last. Headers, if supplied, are ordinary data. Column and order must be integers.

**SORT**(array: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;, columnIndex?: [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput), sortOrder?: [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput)) → [Array](#type-Array)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| array | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |
| columnIndex | [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput) | Default: `0` | See behavior above. |
| sortOrder | [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput) | Default: `1` | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid column/order or numeric conversion; normal spill protection applies.

**Examples:**

```text
=SORT(VSTACK(5,2),0,1)
```

<a id="function-UNIQUE"></a>
### UNIQUE

Keep the first occurrence of each distinct row, preserving source order. Equality is type-sensitive across fields: text "1", number 1 and TRUE are different.

**UNIQUE**(array: [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt;) → [Array](#type-Array)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| array | [Scalar](#type-Scalar) ∣ [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Scalar](#type-Scalar)&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=UNIQUE(VSTACK(2,2,5))
```

<a id="function-CHART"></a>
### CHART

Begin a declarative Chart builder. No build() terminal is needed: a selected chart type renders over the grid. Without a type the cell displays blank. A typed chart requires at least one series; configurations apply in call order. Readable errors are prefixed Chart:.

**CHART**() → [Chart](#type-Chart) ∣ [Text](#type-Text)

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Malformed builder, invalid data or circular source references.

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().line().series(B0:B3)
```

<a id="function-CF"></a>
### CF

Begin a conditional-format builder in the conditional-format pane. Requires range and at least one foreground/background/alignment property. Condition defaults to TRUE. Rules merge per property in order, never mutate values, and persist with the workbook. Not an ordinary cell formula.

**CF**() → [ConditionalRule](#type-ConditionalRule)

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Missing target/style or malformed builder; invalid predicates and colours.

**Examples:**

```text
=CF().range(A0:D3).when([]{}>5).bg("navy")
```

## Stream methods

<a id="method-Stream.filter"></a>
### Stream.filter

Lazily keep items whose one-parameter predicate is true, preserving order and headings. Predicate results use spreadsheet condition conversion.

**Stream.filter**(predicate: (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition)) → [Stream](#type-Stream)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| predicate | (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Returns an empty stream retaining its schema.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).filter(a->a.n>2).toTable()
```

<a id="method-Stream.map"></a>
### Stream.map

Lazily project each item to a scalar, immutable record, or positional row. Record keys become headings; literal record/row projections retain headings even if empty. Fields must be scalar when converted to a table. Inside callbacks + concatenates if either operand is text; otherwise it adds numerically.

**Stream.map**(mapper: (`T`) → `U`) → [Stream](#type-Stream)&lt;`U`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mapper | (`T`) → `U` | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** No mapper invocations. Literal projection schema is retained.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid callback, duplicate/empty/reserved object keys or incompatible table fields.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).map(a->{double:a.n*2}).toTable()
```

<a id="method-Stream.sorted"></a>
### Stream.sorted

Stable sort with a two-parameter comparator returning a finite negative, zero or positive number. Buffers the input when consumed.

**Stream.sorted**(comparator: (`T`, `T`) → [Number](#type-Number)) → [Stream](#type-Stream)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| comparator | (`T`, `T`) → [Number](#type-Number) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Empty stream with original schema.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid comparator or nonfinite comparison result.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).sorted((a,b)->b.n-a.n).toTable()
```

<a id="method-Stream.distinct"></a>
### Stream.distinct

Keep the first structurally equal item, preserving order. Text, numbers and booleans are distinct types; record field order does not affect equality. Retains seen keys, not whole input tables.

**Stream.distinct**() → [Stream](#type-Stream)&lt;`T`&gt;

**Empty input:** Empty stream.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,2,5)).distinct().count()
```

<a id="method-Stream.limit"></a>
### Stream.limit

Keep at most count items. Count must convert to a nonnegative integer. Zero reads no data rows; the source heading still validates. Does not read an item beyond the limit.

**Stream.limit**(count: [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput)) → [Stream](#type-Stream)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count | [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Empty stream.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: negative/nonintegral count.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).limit(1).toTable()
```

<a id="method-Stream.skip"></a>
### Stream.skip

Read and discard the first count items, then yield the rest. Count must convert to a nonnegative integer. Errors in skipped source rows still propagate.

**Stream.skip**(count: [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput)) → [Stream](#type-Stream)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count | [NumericInput](#type-NumericInput) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Empty stream.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: negative/nonintegral count.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).skip(1).toTable()
```

<a id="method-Stream.reduce"></a>
### Stream.reduce

Fold items left-to-right with (accumulator,item)->nextAccumulator. The accumulator must retain the seed type/record schema. Returns the accumulated value directly, never an Optional merely because the input is empty. Records/rows become headed tables only at the cell boundary.

**Stream.reduce**(seed: `A`, reducer: (`A`, `T`) → `A`) → `A`

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| seed | `A` | Required | See behavior above. |
| reducer | (`A`, `T`) → `A` | Required | See behavior above. |

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** Returns seed unchanged.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: invalid reducer or changed accumulator type/schema.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).reduce(10,(total,a)->total+a.n)
```

<a id="method-Stream.toTable"></a>
### Stream.toTable

Materialize a spill table, headings first. Records use their field names; scalars use value; positional rows use column1, column2, …. Optional heading arguments rename columns and must match width. Every item must have consistent fields/width and scalar cells. Without projection, reproduces the source range like always-true FILTER. Maximum output: 1,000,000 cells.

**Stream.toTable**(…heading: [Text](#type-Text)) → [Table](#type-Table)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| heading (variadic) | [Text](#type-Text) | Zero or more | See behavior above. |

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** Headings only. Literal projection headings survive; provide headings for an otherwise unknown empty shape.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: inconsistent shapes, invalid headings or non-scalar fields; #CALC!: too many cells; #SPILL!: collision or sheet bounds.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).toTable()
```

<a id="method-Stream.count"></a>
### Stream.count

Count data items, excluding the heading. Consumes the stream; source errors propagate.

**Stream.count**() → [Number](#type-Number)

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** 0.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).count()
```

<a id="method-Stream.anyMatch"></a>
### Stream.anyMatch

Return TRUE on the first matching item; no later rows are read. Predicate uses spreadsheet condition conversion.

**Stream.anyMatch**(predicate: (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition)) → [Boolean](#type-Boolean)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| predicate | (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** FALSE.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).anyMatch(a->a.n>3)
```

<a id="method-Stream.allMatch"></a>
### Stream.allMatch

Return FALSE on the first nonmatching item; no later rows are read. Predicate uses spreadsheet condition conversion.

**Stream.allMatch**(predicate: (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition)) → [Boolean](#type-Boolean)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| predicate | (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** TRUE (there are no counterexamples).

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).allMatch(a->a.n>0)
```

<a id="method-Stream.noneMatch"></a>
### Stream.noneMatch

Return FALSE on the first matching item; no later rows are read. Equivalent to negating anyMatch.

**Stream.noneMatch**(predicate: (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition)) → [Boolean](#type-Boolean)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| predicate | (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** TRUE.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).noneMatch(a->a.n<0)
```

<a id="method-Stream.findFirst"></a>
### Stream.findFirst

Return the first item wrapped in Optional without reading later items. Retains the actual scalar/record/row for subsequent Optional methods. A blank first item is present, not empty.

**Stream.findFirst**() → [Optional](#type-Optional)&lt;`T`&gt;

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** Optional.empty.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).findFirst().map(a->a.n).orElse(0)
```

<a id="method-Stream.sum"></a>
### Stream.sum

Add the numeric stream items. Map the desired field first. Numeric text and booleans convert; blanks count as zero (including in the average divisor); nonnumeric text errors. Uses decimal arithmetic.

**Stream.sum**() → [Number](#type-Number)

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** 0, the additive identity.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: nonnumeric items; source and arithmetic errors propagate, never become empty.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).map(a->a.n).sum()
```

**Stream terminal:** consumes the pipeline; any following methods belong to the returned type, not the stream.

**Empty input:** Optional.empty, not a calculation error.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: nonnumeric items; source and arithmetic errors propagate, never become empty.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2,5)).map(a->a.n).min().orElse(0)
```

## Optional methods

<a id="method-Optional.map"></a>
### Optional.map

Transform a present value. The mapper is not invoked when empty. Returning an Optional nests it; use flatMap to flatten one level.

**Optional.map**(mapper: (`T`) → `U`) → [Optional](#type-Optional)&lt;`U`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mapper | (`T`) → `U` | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Optional.empty.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2)).findFirst().map(a->a.n*3).orElse(0)
```

<a id="method-Optional.flatMap"></a>
### Optional.flatMap

Transform a present value using a mapper that itself returns Optional. Flattens exactly one level. A non-Optional mapper result is an error.

**Optional.flatMap**(mapper: (`T`) → [Optional](#type-Optional)&lt;`U`&gt;) → [Optional](#type-Optional)&lt;`U`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mapper | (`T`) → [Optional](#type-Optional)&lt;`U`&gt; | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Optional.empty; mapper not invoked.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #VALUE!: mapper did not return Optional.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2)).findFirst().flatMap(a->rowstream(VSTACK("n",a.n)).findFirst()).map(a->a.n).orElse(0)
```

<a id="method-Optional.filter"></a>
### Optional.filter

Keep a present value only if its predicate is true; otherwise return empty. Uses spreadsheet condition conversion.

**Optional.filter**(predicate: (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition)) → [Optional](#type-Optional)&lt;`T`&gt;

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| predicate | (`T`) → [Condition](#type-Condition) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Optional.empty; predicate not invoked.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2)).findFirst().filter(a->a.n>3).isEmpty()
```

<a id="method-Optional.isPresent"></a>
### Optional.isPresent

Test presence without unwrapping. Zero, FALSE and empty text are present.

**Optional.isPresent**() → [Boolean](#type-Boolean)

**Empty input:** FALSE.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",0)).findFirst().isPresent()
```

<a id="method-Optional.isEmpty"></a>
### Optional.isEmpty

Test absence without unwrapping.

**Optional.isEmpty**() → [Boolean](#type-Boolean)

**Empty input:** TRUE.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2)).limit(0).findFirst().isEmpty()
```

<a id="method-Optional.orElse"></a>
### Optional.orElse

Unwrap a present value, or evaluate fallback only when empty. Unlike Java orElse, this is lazy like spreadsheet IF; a separate orElseGet is unnecessary. The fallback supplies the missing result type when empty.

**Optional.orElse**(fallback: `T`) → `T`

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fallback | `T` | Required | Lazy; only evaluated if needed. See behavior above. |

**Empty input:** Evaluates and returns fallback.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2)).map(a->a.n).average().orElse(0)
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2)).findFirst().map(a->a.n).orElse(1/0)
```

<a id="method-Optional.orElseThrow"></a>
### Optional.orElseThrow

Unwrap a present value; explicitly request #N/A if empty. Errors remain distinguishable from an empty Optional.

**Optional.orElseThrow**() → `T`

**Empty input:** Throws #N/A.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- #N/A: Optional is empty.

**Examples:**

```text
=rowstream(VSTACK("n",2)).findFirst().orElseThrow().n
```

## Chart methods

<a id="method-Chart.line"></a>
### Chart.line

Select a line chart; later type calls override earlier ones. Blank y-values leave gaps; zero and negative values are supported.

**Chart.line**() → [Chart](#type-Chart)

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().line().series(B0:B3)
```

<a id="method-Chart.bar"></a>
### Chart.bar

Select a bar chart; later type calls override earlier ones. Blank y-values leave gaps; zero and negative values are supported.

**Chart.bar**() → [Chart](#type-Chart)

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().bar().series(B0:B3)
```

<a id="method-Chart.scatter"></a>
### Chart.scatter

Select a scatter chart; later type calls override earlier ones. Requires finite numeric x-values; points retain source order.

**Chart.scatter**() → [Chart](#type-Chart)

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().scatter().series(B0:B3)
```

<a id="method-Chart.pie"></a>
### Chart.pie

Select a pie chart; later type calls override earlier ones. Requires exactly one series with nonnegative values. Zero/blank values create no slice.

**Chart.pie**() → [Chart](#type-Chart)

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().pie().series(B0:B3)
```

<a id="method-Chart.x"></a>
### Chart.x

Set shared labels or scatter x-values from an ascending single row/column/cell reference. Relative, cross-sheet and named references work. Length must match every series. Default: point numbers starting at 1.

**Chart.x**(labelRange: [Reference](#type-Reference)) → [Chart](#type-Chart)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| labelRange | [Reference](#type-Reference) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Invalid reference/shape, mismatched length, or nonnumeric scatter x-value.

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().bar().x(A0:A3).series(B0:B3)
```

<a id="method-Chart.series"></a>
### Chart.series

Append a series from an ascending single row/column/cell reference. Names are double-quoted text literals, defaulting to Series 1, Series 2, …. All series must have the same length; finite numeric data is required and blanks create gaps. Pie permits one nonnegative series. Source edits recalculate the chart.

**Chart.series**(valueRange: [Reference](#type-Reference), name?: [Text](#type-Text)) → [Chart](#type-Chart)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| valueRange | [Reference](#type-Reference) | Required | See behavior above. |
| name | [Text](#type-Text) | Optional; see behavior | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Invalid/nonfinite data, invalid reference, unequal lengths or invalid pie data.

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().line().series(B0:B3,"Revenue")
```

<a id="method-Chart.title"></a>
### Chart.title

Set title using a double-quoted text literal, not a formula expression. Defaults to empty text. Axis labels are ignored by pie charts. Text is displayed literally, never as HTML.

**Chart.title**(text: [Text](#type-Text)) → [Chart](#type-Chart)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | [Text](#type-Text) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=CHART().line().series(B0:B3).title("Revenue")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | [Text](#type-Text) | Required | See behavior above. |

<a id="method-Chart.size"></a>

Set overall pixel dimensions using positive numeric literals. Defaults to 320 × 200; does not change cell sizes. Later size/width/height calls override the relevant dimensions.

Set nonnegative pixel offsets from the formula cell, using numeric literals. Defaults to (0,0). The chart moves with its cell; no drag-positioning or cell-size changes.

## ConditionalRule methods

<a id="method-ConditionalRule.range"></a>
### ConditionalRule.range

Set the required local absolute target cell/range, such as A0:D3. Endpoints may be reversed. No relative, named or cross-sheet target references. Later calls override earlier ranges; rows and columns are zero-based.

**ConditionalRule.range**(range: [Reference](#type-Reference)) → [ConditionalRule](#type-ConditionalRule)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| range | [Reference](#type-Reference) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Invalid target syntax, unsafe coordinates or out-of-sheet range when installed.

**Examples:**

```text
=CF().range(A0:D3).bg("navy")
```

<a id="method-ConditionalRule.when"></a>
### ConditionalRule.when

Set a formula expression evaluated separately at each target cell. Defaults to TRUE. Relative references resolve from each target. Reads settled decimal values; chart targets are skipped. Only the safe deterministic function subset is available. Predicate errors are reported per cell, not treated as matches.

**ConditionalRule.when**(condition: [Condition](#type-Condition)) → [ConditionalRule](#type-ConditionalRule)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| condition | [Condition](#type-Condition) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Unsafe/malformed expression at definition time; invalid or nonscalar condition at evaluation time.

**Examples:**

```text
=CF().range(A0:D3).when([]{}>5).fg("gold")
```

<a id="method-ConditionalRule.fg"></a>
### ConditionalRule.fg

Set the foreground using a double-quoted CSS named colour or #RGB/#RGBA/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA hex literal. Later matching rules override only properties they supply, without changing stored cell styling.

**ConditionalRule.fg**(colour: [Text](#type-Text)) → [ConditionalRule](#type-ConditionalRule)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| colour | [Text](#type-Text) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Invalid colour or non-quoted literal.

**Examples:**

```text
=CF().range(A0:D3).fg("navy")
```

<a id="method-ConditionalRule.bg"></a>
### ConditionalRule.bg

Set the background using a double-quoted CSS named colour or #RGB/#RGBA/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA hex literal. Later matching rules override only properties they supply, without changing stored cell styling.

**ConditionalRule.bg**(colour: [Text](#type-Text)) → [ConditionalRule](#type-ConditionalRule)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| colour | [Text](#type-Text) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Invalid colour or non-quoted literal.

**Examples:**

```text
=CF().range(A0:D3).bg("navy")
```

<a id="method-ConditionalRule.name"></a>
### ConditionalRule.name

Set an optional rule label using a double-quoted text literal. Defaults to empty text; later calls override it.

**ConditionalRule.name**(text: [Text](#type-Text)) → [ConditionalRule](#type-ConditionalRule)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | [Text](#type-Text) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Examples:**

```text
=CF().range(A0:D3).bg("navy").name("Highlight")
```

<a id="method-ConditionalRule.align"></a>
### ConditionalRule.align

Set alignment to the double-quoted literal auto, left, center or right. Later matching alignment overrides earlier alignment without modifying stored styling.

**ConditionalRule.align**(alignment: [Text](#type-Text)) → [ConditionalRule](#type-ConditionalRule)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| alignment | [Text](#type-Text) | Required | See behavior above. |

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Invalid alignment or non-quoted literal.

**Examples:**


## Mathjs functions

These entries bind the installed mathjs implementation to its own prose, examples and public type declarations; they are not copied implementations. Return types containing Any indicate upstream or runtime uncertainty. Native number/BigNumber are both presented as Number; Matrix/MathArray normalize to spreadsheet Array. Upstream scalar/collection aliases are expanded into structured unions. Original declarations remain visible for details lost by normalization.

Not every upstream overload is usable in a spreadsheet: there is no assignment, general JavaScript callback, multidimensional cell array, arbitrary object access, or executable JavaScript. Library options/objects must come from compatible library producers; a formula record is not an arbitrary JavaScript options object. Upstream examples are reproduced for context and can contain these unsupported constructs; they are not all executable DataFlow examples. Prefer Stream/Optional methods for callbacks. Unsafe engine/configuration functions such as import, evaluate, parse, compile, config and createUnit remain blocked and are not listed as callable functions. Constructors/internal exports that were already reachable are listed transparently, not newly enabled.

<a id="function-abs"></a>
### abs

Compute the absolute value.

**Overload 1**

**abs**(x: [Complex](#type-Complex)) → [Number](#type-Number)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| x | [Complex](#type-Complex) | Required | A number or matrix for which to get the absolute value |

<details><summary>Upstream declaration (before spreadsheet normalization)</summary>

```ts
abs(x: Complex): number
```

</details>

**Overload 2**

**abs**(x: `T`) → `T`

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| x | `T` | Required | A number or matrix for which to get the absolute value |

<details><summary>Upstream declaration (before spreadsheet normalization)</summary>

```ts
abs<T extends MathType>(x: T): T
```

</details>

**Library:** mathjs; available in conditional predicates. Decimal-compatible arguments remain decimals; individual overloads may convert numeric types.

**Registered library input signatures:** `number`; `Complex`; `BigNumber`; `Fraction`; `Unit`; `bigint`; `Array`; `Matrix`.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Library type/domain/shape errors propagate. Spreadsheet inputs use two-dimensional arrays, blank becomes 0, and unresolved Stream/Optional/Lambda or record inputs are rejected. JavaScript callback overloads are unavailable; use stream methods. Native library array outputs must normalize to a nonempty rectangular array of scalar cells.

**Upstream examples:**

```text
=abs(3.5)
=abs(-4.2)
```

<a id="function-diag"></a>
### diag

Create a diagonal matrix or retrieve the diagonal of a matrix. When x is a vector, a matrix with the vector values on the diagonal will be returned. When x is a matrix, a vector with the diagonal values of the matrix is returned. When k is provided, the k-th diagonal will be filled in or retrieved, if k is positive, the values are placed on the super diagonal. When k is negative, the values are placed on the sub diagonal.

<a id="function-diff"></a>
### diff

Create a new matrix or array with the difference of the passed matrix or array.
Dim parameter is optional and used to indicate the dimension of the array/matrix to apply the difference
If no dimension parameter is passed it is assumed as dimension 0
Dimension is zero-based in javascript and one-based in the parser
Arrays must be 'rectangular' meaning arrays like [1, 2]
If something is passed as a matrix it will be returned as a matrix but other than that all matrices are converted to arrays

<a id="function-dot"></a>
### dot

Calculate the dot product of two vectors. The dot product of A = [a1, a2, a3, ..., an] and B = [b1, b2, b3, ..., bn] is defined as dot(A, B) = a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 + a3 * b3 + ... + an * bn

| y | [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Any](#type-Any)&gt; | Required | Co-ordinates of first end-point of second line OR Coefficients of the plane's equation |

<a id="function-slu"></a>
### slu

Calculate the Matrix LU decomposition with full pivoting. Matrix A is decomposed in two matrices (L, U) and two permutation vectors (pinv, q) where P * A * Q = L * U

**slu**(A: [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Any](#type-Any)&gt;, order: [Number](#type-Number), threshold: [Number](#type-Number)) → [Math.SLUDecomposition](#type-Math.SLUDecomposition)

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | [Array](#type-Array)&lt;[Any](#type-Any)&gt; | Required | A two dimensional sparse matrix for which to get the LU decomposition. |
| order | [Number](#type-Number) | Required | The Symbolic Ordering and Analysis order: 0 - Natural ordering, no permutation vector q is returned 1 - Matrix must be square, symbolic ordering and analysis is performed on M = A + A' 2 - Symbolic ordering and analysis is performed on M = A' * A. Dense columns from A' are dropped, A recreated from A'. This is appropriate for LU factorization of non-symmetric matrices. 3 - Symbolic ordering and analysis is performed on M = A' * A. This is best used for LU factorization is matrix M has no dense rows. A dense row is a row with more than 10*sqr(columns) entries. |
| threshold | [Number](#type-Number) | Required | Partial pivoting threshold (1 for partial pivoting) |

<details><summary>Upstream declaration (before spreadsheet normalization)</summary>

```ts

```

</details>

<a id="function-subset"></a>
### subset

Get or set a subset of the entries of a matrix or characters of a string. Indexes are one-based. There should be one index specification for each dimension of the target. Each specification can be a single index, a list of indices, or a range in colon notation `l:u`. In a range, both the lower bound l and upper bound u are included; and if a bound is omitted it defaults to the most extreme valid value. The cartesian product of the indices specified in each dimension determines the target of the operation.

**subset**(value: `T`, index: [Math.Index](#type-Math.Index), replacement?: [Any](#type-Any), defaultValue?: [Any](#type-Any)) → `T`

| Parameter | Type | Required/default | Evaluation / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `T` | Required | An array, matrix, or string |
| index | [Math.Index](#type-Math.Index) | Required | For each dimension, an index or list of indices to get or set. |
| replacement | [Any](#type-Any) | Optional; see behavior | An array, matrix, or scalar. If provided, the subset is replaced with replacement. If not provided, the subset is returned |
| defaultValue | [Any](#type-Any) | Optional; see behavior | Default value, filled in on new entries when the matrix is resized. If not provided, math.matrix elements will be left undefined. Default value: undefined. |

<details><summary>Upstream declaration (before spreadsheet normalization)</summary>

```ts
subset<T extends MathCollection | string>( value: T, index: Index, replacement?: any, defaultValue?: any ): T
```

</details>

**Library:** mathjs; unavailable in conditional predicates. Decimal-compatible arguments remain decimals; individual overloads may convert numeric types.

**Registered library input signatures:** `Matrix,Index`; `Array,Index`; `Object,Index`; `string,Index`; `Matrix,Index,any,any`; `Array,Index,any,any`; `Array,Index,any`; `Matrix,Index,any`; `string,Index,string`; `string,Index,string,string`; `Object,Index,any`.

**Errors / restrictions:**
- Library type/domain/shape errors propagate. Spreadsheet inputs use two-dimensional arrays, blank becomes 0, and unresolved Stream/Optional/Lambda or record inputs are rejected. JavaScript callback overloads are unavailable; use stream methods. Native library array outputs must normalize to a nonempty rectangular array of scalar cells.

```text
=f[2, 1]
```


## Maintaining definitions

Own each function/method's implementation, typed parameters, return descriptor, behavior, errors, empty-input rules and examples together. Types implement accepts(value), present(value, context), and a safe method registry. Presentation returns a scalar/table/record/chart model or an explanatory error; the spreadsheet owns placement and rendering. Type names are human-readable labels only: signatures reference FormulaType objects, and generic binding uses descriptor identity. Runtime checks validate callback arity, method arguments, Optional results and reducer accumulator schemas; existing spreadsheet/library functions retain their own conversion/domain checks.

Change definitions in src/classes/FormulaFunctions.js, ChartFormula.js, ConditionalFormatting.js or FormulaTypes.js. Run npm run docs:generate to rebuild this reference and the structured mathjs overload bindings from the installed dependency. npm run docs:check (also exercised by tests) rejects stale generated output. Autocomplete reads the same registries, including the return type after a terminal; there is no separately maintained help table.
